keyEvents.event: The Nakba: some 700,000 Palestinians flee or are expelled during the first Arab-Israeli war
keyEvents.impact: Refugee identity and the right of return became the core of Palestinian nationalism

keyEvents.event: Israel occupies the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza
keyEvents.impact: Began an occupation that has outlasted every peace process

keyEvents.event: First Intifada and founding of Hamas
keyEvents.impact: Grassroots revolt forced recognition of the PLO and created its Islamist rival

keyEvents.event: Oslo Accords create the Palestinian Authority
keyEvents.impact: Limited self-rule without statehood; settlements kept expanding

keyEvents.event: Hamas seizes Gaza after winning 2006 elections; Israeli-Egyptian blockade follows
keyEvents.impact: Split between a Fatah-run West Bank and a Hamas-run Gaza; no national elections since 2006

keyEvents.event: Hamas's October 7 attack on Israel triggers the Gaza war
keyEvents.impact: Tens of thousands killed, most of Gaza destroyed, famine conditions, and a genocide case at the ICJ

keyEvents.event: Wave of Western recognitions (France, UK, Canada, Australia); Trump-brokered Gaza ceasefire in October and UN Resolution 2803
keyEvents.impact: Diplomatic high-water mark for statehood while Gaza is split along Israel's 'yellow line'

keyEvents.event: Phase two: technocratic Gaza committee and stalled International Stabilization Force; Hamas refuses to disarm; PA elections slip
keyEvents.impact: Gaza remains a frozen war zone with Israel holding well over half the strip; West Bank settler violence surges

history.narrative: A stateless nation split between an aging, aid-dependent Palestinian Authority in the West Bank and a battered but undefeated Hamas in Gaza. It wields more diplomatic recognition than ever and less control over its own territory than at any time since Oslo.

redLines.description: Formal Israeli annexation of the West Bank or Jordan Valley
Permanent expulsion of Gaza's population or annexation of the strip
Imposed governance that excludes Palestinians or renounces statehood and the right of return

internalDivisions.name: Fatah-Hamas schism between the West Bank and Gaza
Gaza's humanitarian catastrophe and clan militias versus the West Bank
Youth alienation from the aging PA leadership and its security cooperation with Israel

goals.description: Achieve an internationally recognized independent state on the 1967 lines with East Jerusalem
Secure Gaza reconstruction funding and end the humanitarian catastrophe
Reunify Gaza and the West Bank under a single Palestinian authority
Win full UN membership and further recognitions to isolate Israeli annexation
